text:
arjun: quick heads-up — after the kernel-selection RFC follow-up, I ran some traces and the churn from very fine-grained seq-len bucketing is the main source of kernel thrash on p4s.

marta: can you summarise numbers? is it more latency p99 or GPU SM churn?

arjun: mostly SM churn leading to tail latency spikes. 1) we keep compiling/choosing slightly different kernels as batches vary by 5-10 tokens, 2) warmup prefill budgets don't converge fast enough for short bursts. example: a 3s spike with 90% short seqs then back to long tails.

lia: is this the case where current bucket boundaries are at every 8 tokens?

arjun: yeah. boundaries at [32,40,48,...] — too many tiny buckets. Switching to quantile-based coarse buckets (e.g., q10) reduced kernel flips in sim by ~60%.

zach: nice — what's the perf delta for steady-state throughput? sometimes coarser buckets hurt packing efficiency.

arjun: throughput dips ~2% on synthetic steady traffic with tight seqlen distribution, but p99 latency improves by ~20ms on bursts. tradeoff seems worth it for multi-tenant clusters.

marta: we should also look at batch-shape hysteresis: avoid switching kernel unless candidate reduces estimated cost by X% or after N requests.

lia: +1. my thought: add a cheap heuristic in runtime that requires two conditions: 1) new kernel wins on expected cost by at least 7%, 2) observed sequence distribution persists for >= 5s or >= 50 requests. that should stop micro-flips.

arjun: proposed policy makes sense. also want to tweak warmup prefill: give a short fast-path prefill for tiny seqs so cache/KV prefill doesn't force a full kernel switch.

zach: curious about eviction: current prefill cache TTL is global 10s. for tenants with bursty traffic, that's too short — we evict and then pay warmup again. can we make TTL tenant-weighted?

marta: we could compute tenant affinity score (recent QPS * avg seq_len) and multiply TTL by factor in [0.5,4]. heavier tenants keep entries longer.

arjun: downside: long TTLs can increase memory pressure. need an eviction budget across all tenants (LRU + weighted cap).

autotune-bot: perf-metric-report: kernel_flip_rate reduced by 58% in sim-run-2026-04-12 when using q10 buckets + hysteresis.

lia: action items:
- arjun: implement 2-stage policy (coarse quantile buckets + fallback dynamic splitter) behind feature flag (ft.autotune.coarse_buckets). target perf test by EOD Friday.
- marta: add hysteresis thresholds to kernel selector config and expose experiment knobs: cost_delta_pct, min_persistence_secs.
- zach: run memory pressure sim to validate tenant-weighted TTL and propose global eviction budget.

marta: small config sketch (we can iterate):
```
kernel_selector:
  bucket_mode: quantile
  quantiles: 10
  cost_delta_pct: 7
  min_persistence_secs: 5
  prefill_fastpath_max_seq: 64
  tenant_ttl_factor_bounds: [0.5, 4.0]
```

arjun: +1 to that YAML. also we should add telemetry events for: kernel_choice_change, kernel_flip_rejected(reason), prefill_fastpath_used. minimal to start.

zach: for experiments, suggest canary 2% of traffic on a dedicated pool for one week, capture p50/p95/p99, kernel_flip_rate, memory_reservations, cold_start_warmup_cost.

lia: I'll create the canary pool and hook metrics dashboards. also, ensure canary tenants have mixed seq-len histograms to test tails.

arjun: one more question — how do we handle model-variant compatibility when switching kernels? some quantized kernels only support certain weight layouts.

marta: keep compatibility table in catalog; kernel_selector will only consider compatible kernels. if none compatible, fallback to generic kernel (slower). we should log a specific telemetry tag for "compatibility_fallback".

arjun: perfect. ok I'll land a small prototype and share a PR. please keep discussion on this thread for decisions.

marta: cool, ping @lia @zach when PR is up. I'll review selector semantics. :thumbsup:

zach: thanks — I'll prepare the sim configs and load-gen.

autotune-bot: note: RFC follow-up checklist updated: added "coarse-buckets + hysteresis" experiment.

arjun: thanks all. short-term goal: reduce kernel flips without meaningful throughput loss. long-term: consider model-aware bucket shapes (per-model quantiles) if this goes well.
